query: What drives customer satisfaction (Overall Rating) across the different airlines?

per_column.name: Average_Service_Rating
per_column.rationale: A composite of the sub-rating columns; gives a useful aggregate service axis to relate to Overall Rating. Values are directly derivable from the rating columns and match samples plausibly.

per_column.name: Service_Consistency
per_column.rationale: Standard deviation across the service dimensions; a genuine new axis (variance vs mean) that could explain satisfaction. Computed from existing rating columns, so well grounded.

per_column.name: Lowest_Rated_Dimension
per_column.rationale: Identifies the weakest service axis per review — directly useful for diagnosing satisfaction drivers. Derived from the sub-rating columns. Sample 1 (a glowing review picking Inflight Entertainment as lowest) is plausible if that dimension simply had the numerically lowest score.

per_column.name: Poor_Dimensions_Count
per_column.rationale: Counts how many dimensions fall below a threshold; a useful severity/breadth measure for modeling dissatisfaction. Derivable from existing rating columns and consistent with samples.

per_column.name: Review_Length
per_column.rationale: Raw character length of review text — a generic surface feature explicitly flagged as low-leverage. Values are trivially derivable from the text but add little analytical value for what drives satisfaction.

per_column.name: Review_Word_Count
per_column.rationale: Token count; near-redundant with Review_Length and generic. Grounded but adds negligible analytical leverage for this query.

per_column.name: Is_Premium_Class
per_column.rationale: Binary flag derived from the Class column; a clean grouping axis to compare satisfaction across cabin tiers. Sample 4 (Business Class mentioned in text) correctly flagged premium.

per_column.name: Traveler_Category
per_column.rationale: Traveler segmentation is a useful grouping axis, but the mapping is questionable: sample 1 (no party info in text) labeled 'Group', sample 3 (a couple/family return trip) labeled 'Group', while sample 2 labeled 'Solo' without clear support. Likely derived from Type of Traveller column but several assignments look under-supported.

per_column.name: Review_Verified
per_column.rationale: A numeric restatement of the existing Verified column — trivially redundant with an original column, so low added leverage. Values are grounded.

judge.rationale: Most columns are well-grounded, being computed from existing rating/class/traveller fields. The rating-derived composites (Average_Service_Rating, Service_Consistency, Lowest_Rated_Dimension, Poor_Dimensions_Count) and the class/traveller groupings provide genuine new axes for explaining Overall Rating. Weak spots: Review_Length and Review_Word_Count are generic surface features with little leverage, Review_Verified merely restates an original column, and Traveler_Category shows some under-supported category assignments in the samples.
